about: Fifteen small pure functions of the kind session-map really has (5 easy, 5 medium, 5 hard). The model gets spec and signature and answers {"code": "<a complete ESM module exporting the function>"}. Score: the module is saved as solution.mjs next to the tests saved as solution.test.mjs, in a fresh temp folder, and run with node --test under --permission (read and write only that folder); all tests passing is a correct answer. reference is a known-good solution, used only to prove the tests right.

items.title: Parse a checklist line with an item code
items.spec:
Parse one line of a markdown checklist, as used in the project's architecture documents.

A checklist line is: optional leading whitespace, a bullet ('-' or '*'), one or more spaces, a box ('[ ]' for open, '[x]' or '[X]' for done), one or more whitespace characters, then the text.

Trim the text. If the trimmed text starts with an item code in backticks, return the code without the backticks and the rest of the text (trimmed) as text. An item code is one or more lowercase letters a-z followed by one or more digits, like `or12` or `fd3`; a backticked token of any other shape (like `npm test` or `OR12`) is not a code and stays part of the text. When there is no code, code is null and text is the whole trimmed text.

Return null for any line that is not a checklist line, and also when there is neither a code nor any text after the box. A line with a code and nothing after it is valid (text is '').
items.signature: export function parseChecklistLine(line: string): { done: boolean, code: string | null, text: string } | null

items.title: Normalize a Windows path into a map key
items.spec:
Normalize a Windows or POSIX path into the form the project uses as a map key.

- Every backslash becomes a forward slash.
- A drive letter at the very start is lowercased ('C:' becomes 'c:'); the rest of the path keeps its case.
- Runs of two or more slashes collapse into one, except that a path that starts with two or more slashes is a network (UNC) path and starts with exactly '//' ('\\server\share' becomes '//server/share').
- A trailing slash is removed, except for a root: 'c:/' and '/' keep it.
- '.' and '..' segments are kept as they are (no resolving).
- An empty string stays empty.

items.title: Format a cost in dollars for the screen
items.spec:
Format a cost in US dollars for display.

- '$' then the amount rounded to cents, with exactly two decimals and a comma every three digits in the whole part: 1234.5 gives '$1,234.50', 999.999 gives '$1,000.00'.
- Rounding to cents is Math.round(Math.abs(n) * 100) on the number as JavaScript holds it: 2.675 gives '$2.68', 0.125 gives '$0.13', and 1.005 (held as 1.00499...) gives '$1.00'. Amounts of 10^13 dollars or more are out of scope.
- Zero gives '$0.00'.
- A positive amount below half a cent (n > 0 and n < 0.005) gives '<$0.01'.
- A negative amount gives a minus before the dollar sign: -1.2 gives '-$1.20'. A negative amount that rounds to zero cents gives '$0.00'.
- Anything that is not a finite number (NaN, Infinity, null, undefined, a numeric string such as '3') gives '—' (an em dash, U+2014).

items.title: Hide CPF numbers in a text
items.spec:
Replace every Brazilian CPF number in a text with '[CPF]' before the text is sent to an outside service.

A CPF is written either as 11 digits in a row ('12345678909') or formatted exactly as ddd.ddd.ddd-dd ('123.456.789-09'). It only counts when it is not glued to more digits: the character right before it and the character right after it (when there is one) must not be a digit 0-9. A run of 12 or more digits, a run of 10 or fewer, and half-formatted forms such as '123456789-09' are left alone. Do not check the verification digits. Everything else in the text stays exactly as it was.

items.title: Make a short card title from a first message
items.spec:
Make a short title for a conversation card from the conversation's first message. max is an integer of at least 2; lengths are JavaScript string lengths.

1. Take the first line (lines are split on '\n') that has a non-whitespace character. If there is none, return ''.
2. Replace every run of whitespace in it (spaces, tabs, '\r') with one space and trim it.
3. If the result is at most max characters long, return it.
4. Otherwise the result is a head plus '…' (one character, U+2026) and must be at most max characters long. The head is the text before the last space found within the first max characters, with every trailing space and punctuation mark among , ; : . - removed from its end (strip them repeatedly, in any order, until the head ends in another character or is empty). If there is no such space (the first word alone is too long), or the head ends up empty, the head is the first max - 1 characters instead.
items.signature: export function shortTitle(text: string, max: number): string

items.title: Merge the cost per day across projects
items.spec:
Merge the daily cost of several projects into one timeline.

Input: an array of { project, days }, where days maps a day written 'YYYY-MM-DD' to a cost in dollars. The same project may appear more than once in the array: add its numbers together. Ignore every value that is not a finite number greater than or equal to 0 (NaN, Infinity, negative numbers, strings, null).

Output: an array of { day, total, byProject }, sorted by day ascending, with one entry for each day that has at least one valid value (a valid 0 counts). byProject maps a project name to that project's cost on that day and lists only projects with at least one valid value that day. total is the sum of that day's valid values. Round total and every byProject value to 4 decimals with Math.round(x * 10000) / 10000, after summing. An empty input gives []. Do not modify the input.
items.signature: export function mergeDailyCost(projects: Array<{ project: string, days: Record<string, number> }>): Array<{ day: string, total: number, byProject: Record<string, number> }>

items.title: Pick a model and effort from task kind and size
items.spec:
Pick the AI model and the reasoning effort for a task.

kind is one of 'search', 'mechanical', 'logic', 'architecture', 'review'. size is one of 'trivial', 'small', 'medium', 'large'. sensitive is an optional boolean (missing means false).

Apply these rules in order; the first that applies decides:
1. kind or size is not in its list: throw a TypeError whose message contains the bad value.
2. kind 'review': { model: 'opus', effort: 'xhigh' }, but effort 'max' when size is 'large'.
3. kind 'architecture', or sensitive is true: { model: 'opus', effort: 'high' }.
4. size 'trivial': { model: 'haiku', effort: 'low' }.
5. kind 'search': haiku / low. kind 'mechanical': sonnet / medium. kind 'logic': sonnet / high, but opus / high when size is 'large'.

Return a new object { model, effort } every time.
items.signature: export function pickModel(task: { kind: string, size: string, sensitive?: boolean }): { model: string, effort: string }

items.title: Debounce alerts by key and time
items.spec:
Decide which alerts to deliver so the owner is not flooded. Each event is { key, at } where at is a time in milliseconds; the array may be in any order.

Process the events by at ascending; events with the same at keep their order from the input. An event is delivered unless an event with the same key was delivered less than windowMs earlier (at - lastDeliveredAt < windowMs means it is suppressed; exactly windowMs apart is delivered). Suppressed events do not restart the window: only delivered events count. Different keys never affect each other. windowMs 0 delivers everything.

Return the delivered events themselves (the same objects, not copies) in processing order. Do not modify the input array or its events.
items.signature: export function debounceAlerts(events: Array<{ key: string, at: number }>, windowMs: number): Array<{ key: string, at: number }>

items.title: Rank conversations by state and recency
items.spec:
Order the conversation cards on the board. Each conversation is { id, state, lastActivity }, where lastActivity is a time in milliseconds (a finite number) or a date string readable by Date.parse. now is the current time in milliseconds.

1. Group by state, in this order: 'waiting' (needs the owner), 'working', 'idle', 'done', then any other state.
2. A 'working' conversation whose last activity is more than 30 minutes before now (now - time > 1800000; exactly 30 minutes still counts as working) belongs to the 'idle' group.
3. Inside a group, the most recent activity comes first; equal times are ordered by id ascending with plain string comparison (<).
4. A lastActivity that cannot be read as a time (an invalid string, NaN, null, missing) counts as the oldest possible time.

Return the ids in that order. Do not modify the input.
items.signature: export function rankConversations(convs: Array<{ id: string, state: string, lastActivity: number | string }>, now: number): string[]

items.title: Parse the command line of a small tool
items.spec:
Parse the command-line arguments of a small tool, like `node run.mjs --kinds code,review --limit 3 --dry-run`. spec maps each option name (without the dashes) to its type: 'boolean', 'string', 'number' or 'list'.

- An argument that starts with '--' is an option, written '--name' or '--name=value'. An option whose name is not in spec throws.
- A boolean option given as '--name' is true; '--name=true' and '--name=false' are accepted; any other '=value' throws.
- A non-boolean option takes its value after '=' or, without '=', from the next argument. It is missing when there is no next argument, when the next argument starts with '--', or when the value (after '=' or taken from the next argument) is the empty string; a missing value throws. The next argument may start with a single '-' (so '--limit -3' is -3).
- 'number': the value must give a finite number with Number(value), else throw. 'list': split the value on commas, trim every piece, drop empty pieces. 'string': the value as is.
- A later repeat of an option overrides the earlier one.
- Every argument that does not start with '--' (and is not an option's value) is positional and goes, in order, into the array '_'. A bare '--' ends the options: every argument after it is positional, even if it starts with '--'.
- Options never given are absent from the result (no defaults).
- Every error thrown is an Error whose message contains the option name.

Return { _: [...positional], ...options }.
items.signature: export function parseArgs(argv: string[], spec: Record<string, 'boolean' | 'string' | 'number' | 'list'>): { _: string[], [name: string]: unknown }

items.title: Split a long document at its headings
items.spec:
Split a markdown document into chunks small enough for a model with a small window.

1. Replace every '\r\n' with '\n', then work line by line (split on '\n').
2. Fences: a line whose first non-whitespace characters are three backticks (```) opens a fenced code block, and the next such line closes it. A fence line itself is never a heading.
3. A heading line is a line that starts (at its very first character) with 1 to 6 '#' characters followed by a space, and is not inside a fenced code block. So '#tag', '####### seven' and '  # indented' are not headings.
4. Cut the document before every heading line: each section starts with its heading and runs until the next heading. The text before the first heading is a section of its own.
5. For each section (its lines joined with '\n'): remove the '\n' characters at its start, then apply trimEnd(). Drop the section if nothing is left.
6. A section of at most maxChars characters is one chunk. A longer section is split into paragraphs at every run of two or more '\n' (blank lines inside fences count too), and the paragraphs are packed greedily, in order, joined by '\n\n', into chunks of at most maxChars characters: a paragraph is added to the current chunk when the result stays within maxChars, otherwise it starts a new chunk. A paragraph longer than maxChars is a chunk on its own; never cut inside a paragraph.

Return all chunks in document order.
items.signature: export function splitAtHeadings(md: string, maxChars: number): string[]

items.title: Turn a file glob into a regular expression
items.spec:
Turn a file glob into a RegExp that tests a whole path written with forward slashes (like 'server/ai/runner.mjs'). The RegExp is anchored at both ends (it must match the entire path) and is case-sensitive.

- '**' that is a whole path segment (at the start or right after '/', and at the end or right before '/') matches whole folders:
  - '**/' matches zero or more leading folders: 'a/**/b' matches 'a/b', 'a/x/b' and 'a/x/y/b'; '**/b' matches 'b' and 'x/y/b'.
  - a final '/**' matches everything below, at least one more character: 'docs/**' matches 'docs/a' and 'docs/a/b' but not 'docs' or 'docs/'.
  - a glob that is just '**' matches every path.
- '**' that is not a whole segment (like 'a**b') behaves like '*'.
- '*' matches any run of characters except '/', possibly empty.
- '?' matches exactly one character that is not '/'.
- '{a,b,c}' matches any one of the comma-separated alternatives; each alternative is literal text and may be empty ('{,x}a' matches 'a' and 'xa'); no nesting. A '{' with no later '}' is a literal '{'.
- Every other character matches itself literally, including characters that are special in regular expressions such as . + ( ) $ ^ | [ ] \.

items.title: Pull the JSON object out of a model's answer
items.spec:
Pull the JSON object out of an AI model's answer. The answer may wrap the object in prose and/or a markdown code fence (```json ... ``` or ``` ... ```).

Find the first '{' in the text and its matching '}': count nested '{' and '}', but ignore every brace inside a JSON string. Strings start and end with a double quote; inside a string, a backslash escapes the next character (so \" does not end the string). Braces and quotes before the first '{' are not looked at. JSON.parse the slice from that '{' to its matching '}' and return { ok: true, value }.

Return { ok: false, error } with error a non-empty string when: text is not a string, there is no '{', the first '{' has no matching '}', or the slice does not parse. Only the first top-level object is considered, even when a later one would parse. Never throw.
items.signature: export function extractJSON(text: string): { ok: true, value: object } | { ok: false, error: string }
